<h1 id="c-code-reviews">C# Code Reviews</h1>
<h2 id="style-guide">Style Guide</h2>
<p>Developers should follow Microsoft's <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/coding-style/coding-conventions">C# Coding Conventions</a> and, where applicable, Microsoft's <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/security/secure-coding-guidelines">Secure Coding Guidelines</a>.</p>
<h2 id="code-analysis-linting">Code Analysis / Linting</h2>
<p>We strongly believe that consistent style increases readability and maintainability of a code base. Hence, we are recommending analyzers / linters to enforce consistency and style rules.</p>
<h3 id="project-setup">Project Setup</h3>
<p>We recommend using a common setup for your solution that you can refer to in all the projects that are part of the solution. Create a <code>common.props</code> file that contains the defaults for all of your projects:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">&lt;Project&gt;</span>
...
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&lt;ItemGroup&gt;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">&lt;PackageReference</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Include=</span><span class="s">&quot;Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers&quot;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Version=</span><span class="s">&quot;5.0.3&quot;</span><span class="nt">&gt;</span>
<span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">&lt;PrivateAssets&gt;</span>all<span class="nt">&lt;/PrivateAssets&gt;</span>
<span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">&lt;IncludeAssets&gt;</span>runtime;<span class="w"> </span>build;<span class="w"> </span>native;<span class="w"> </span>contentfiles;<span class="w"> </span>analyzers;<span class="w"> </span>buildtransitive<span class="nt">&lt;/IncludeAssets&gt;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">&lt;/PackageReference&gt;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">&lt;PackageReference</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Include=</span><span class="s">&quot;StyleCop.Analyzers&quot;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Version=</span><span class="s">&quot;1.1.118&quot;</span><span class="nt">&gt;</span>
<span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">&lt;PrivateAssets&gt;</span>all<span class="nt">&lt;/PrivateAssets&gt;</span>
<span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">&lt;IncludeAssets&gt;</span>runtime;<span class="w"> </span>build;<span class="w"> </span>native;<span class="w"> </span>contentfiles;<span class="w"> </span>analyzers;<span class="w"> </span>buildtransitive<span class="nt">&lt;/IncludeAssets&gt;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">&lt;/PackageReference&gt;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&lt;/ItemGroup&gt;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&lt;PropertyGroup&gt;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">&lt;TreatWarningsAsErrors&gt;</span>true<span class="nt">&lt;/TreatWarningsAsErrors&gt;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&lt;/PropertyGroup&gt;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&lt;ItemGroup</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Condition=</span><span class="s">&quot;Exists(&#39;$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../.editorconfig&#39;)&quot;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">&gt;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">&lt;AdditionalFiles</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Include=</span><span class="s">&quot;$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../.editorconfig&quot;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&lt;/ItemGroup&gt;</span>
...
<span class="nt">&lt;/Project&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>You can then reference the <code>common.props</code> in your other project files to ensure a consistent setup.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">&lt;Project</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Sdk=</span><span class="s">&quot;Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web&quot;</span><span class="nt">&gt;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">&lt;Import</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="na">Project=</span><span class="s">&quot;..\common.props&quot;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
<span class="nt">&lt;/Project&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/ide/editorconfig-code-style-settings-reference?view=vs-2019">.editorconfig</a> allows for configuration and overrides of rules. You can have an .editorconfig file at project level to customize rules for different projects (test projects for example).</p>
<p><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/code-quality/use-roslyn-analyzers?view=vs-2019">Details about the configuration of different rules</a>.</p>
<h3 id="net-analyzers">.NET analyzers</h3>
<p>Microsoft's .NET analyzers has code quality rules and .NET API usage rules implemented as analyzers using the .NET Compiler Platform (Roslyn). This is the replacement for Microsoft's legacy FxCop analyzers.</p>
<p><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/code-quality/install-net-analyzers?view=vs-2019">Enable or install first-party .NET analyzers</a>.</p>
<p>If you are currently using the legacy FxCop analyzers, <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/code-quality/migrate-from-fxcop-analyzers-to-net-analyzers?view=vs-2019">migrate from FxCop analyzers to .NET analyzers</a>.</p>
<h3 id="stylecop-analyzer">StyleCop Analyzer</h3>
<p>The StyleCop analyzer is a nuget package (StyleCop.Analyzers) that can be installed in any of your projects. It's mainly around code style rules and makes sure the team is following the same rules without having subjective discussions about braces and spaces. Detailed information can be found here: <a href="https://github.com/DotNetAnalyzers/StyleCopAnalyzers">StyleCop Analyzers for the .NET Compiler Platform</a>.</p>
<p>The minimum rules set teams should adopt is the <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/code-quality/managed-minimum-rules-rule-set-for-managed-code?view=vs-2022">Managed Recommended Rules</a> rule set.</p>
<h2 id="automatic-code-formatting">Automatic Code Formatting</h2>
<p>Use .editorconfig to configure code formatting rules in your project.</p>
<h2 id="build-validation">Build Validation</h2>
<p>It's important that you enforce your code style and rules in the CI to avoid any team member merging code that does not comply with your standards into your git repo.</p>
<p>If you are using FxCop analyzers and StyleCop analyzer, it's very simple to enable those in the CI. You have to make sure you are setting up the project using nuget and .editorconfig (<a href="#project-setup">see Project setup</a>). Once you have this setup, you will have to configure the pipeline to build your code. That's pretty much it. The FxCop analyzers will run and report the result in your build pipeline. If there are rules that are violated, your build will be red.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">DotNetCoreCLI@2</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Style</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">Check</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">&amp;</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">Build&#39;</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">command</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;build&#39;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">projects</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;**/*.csproj&#39;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="enable-roslyn-support-in-vscode">Enable Roslyn Support in VSCode</h2>
<p>The above steps also work in VS Code provided you enable Roslyn support for Omnisharp. The setting is <code>omnisharp.enableRoslynAnalyzers</code> and must be set to <code>true</code>. After enabling this setting you must "Restart Omnisharp" (this can be done from the Command Palette in VS Code or by restarting VS Code).</p>
<p><img alt="rosyln-support" src="../images/vscode-roslyn.png" /></p>
<h2 id="code-review-checklist">Code Review Checklist</h2>
<p>In addition to the <a href="../../process-guidance/reviewer-guidance/">Code Review Checklist</a> you should also look for these C# specific code review items</p>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code make correct use of <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/concepts/async/#BKMK_AsyncandAwait">asynchronous programming constructs</a>, including proper use of <code>await</code> and <code>Task.WhenAll</code> including CancellationTokens?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the code subject to concurrency issues? Are shared objects properly protected?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is dependency injection (DI) used? Is it setup correctly?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/middleware/index?view=aspnetcore-2.1&amp;tabs=aspnetcore2x">middleware</a> included in this project configured correctly?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are resources released deterministically using the IDispose pattern? Are all disposable objects properly disposed (<a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/using-statement">using pattern</a>)?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the code creating a lot of short-lived objects. Could we optimize GC pressure?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the code written in a way that causes boxing operations to happen?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does the code <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/exceptions/best-practices-for-exceptions">handle exceptions correctly</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is package management being used (NuGet) instead of committing DLLs?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code use LINQ appropriately? Pulling LINQ into a project to replace a single short loop or in ways that do not perform well are usually not appropriate.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code properly validate arguments sanity (i.e. <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/quality-rules/ca1062">CA1062</a>)? Consider leveraging extensions such as <a href="https://github.com/danielwertheim/Ensure.That">Ensure.That</a></li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code include telemetry (<a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/app-insights-overview">metrics, tracing</a> and <a href="https://serilog.net/">logging</a>) instrumentation?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code leverage the <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/configuration/options?view=aspnetcore-3.1">options design pattern</a> by using classes to provide strongly typed access to groups of related settings?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Instead of using raw strings, are constants used in the main class? Or if these strings are used across files/classes, is there a static class for the constants?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are magic numbers explained? There should be no number in the code without at least a comment of why this is here. If the number is repetitive, is there a constant/enum or equivalent?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is proper exception handling set up? Catching the exception base class (<code>catch (Exception)</code>) is generally not the right pattern. Instead, catch the specific exceptions that can happen e.g., <code>IOException</code>.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the use of #pragma fair?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are tests arranged correctly with the <strong>Arrange/Act/Assert</strong> pattern and properly documented in this way?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> If there is an asynchronous method, does the name of the method end with the <code>Async</code> suffix?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> If a method is asynchronous, is <code>Task.Delay</code> used instead of <code>Thread.Sleep</code>? <code>Task.Delay</code> is not blocking the current thread and creates a task that will complete without blocking the thread, so in a multi-threaded, multi-task environment, this is the one to prefer.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is a cancellation token for asynchronous tasks needed rather than bool patterns?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is a minimum level of logging in place? Are the logging levels used sensible?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are internal vs private vs public classes and methods used the right way?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are auto property set and get used the right way? In a model without constructor and for deserialization, it is ok to have all accessible. For other classes usually a private set or internal set is better.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the <code>using</code> pattern for streams and other disposable classes used? If not, better to have the <code>Dispose</code> method called explicitly.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are the classes that maintain collections in memory, thread safe? When used under concurrency, use lock pattern.</li>
</ul>

<h1 id="go-code-reviews">Go Code Reviews</h1>
<h2 id="style-guide">Style Guide</h2>
<p>Developers should follow the <a href="https://golang.org/doc/effective_go.html">Effective Go</a> Style Guide.</p>
<h2 id="code-analysis-linting">Code Analysis / Linting</h2>
<h3 id="project-setup">Project Setup</h3>
<p>Below is the project setup that you would like to have in your VS Code.</p>
<h4 id="vscode-go-extension">VSCode go Extension</h4>
<p>Using the Go extension for Visual Studio Code, you get language features like IntelliSense, code navigation, symbol search, bracket matching, snippets, etc. This extension includes rich language support for go in VS Code.</p>
<h4 id="go-vet">go vet</h4>
<p><code>go vet</code> is a static analysis tool that checks for common go errors, such as incorrect use of range loop variables or misaligned printf arguments. Go code should be able to build with no <code>go vet</code> errors. This will be part of vscode-go extension.</p>
<h4 id="golint">golint</h4>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> The golint library is deprecated and archived.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>The linter revive (below) might be a suitable replacement.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/golang/lint">golint</a> can be an effective tool for finding many issues, but it errors on the side of false positives. It is best used by developers when working on code, not as part of an automated build process. This is the default linter which is set up as part of the vscode-go extension.</p>
<h4 id="revive">revive</h4>
<p><a href="https://revive.run/">Revive</a> is a linter for go, it provides a framework for development of custom rules, and lets you define a strict preset for enhancing your development &amp; code review processes.</p>
<h2 id="automatic-code-formatting">Automatic Code Formatting</h2>
<h3 id="gofmt">gofmt</h3>
<p><code>gofmt</code> is the automated code format style guide for Go. This is part of the vs-code extension, and it is enabled by default to run on save of every file.</p>
<h2 id="aggregator">Aggregator</h2>
<h3 id="golangci-lint">golangci-lint</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/">golangci-lint</a> is the replacement for the now deprecated <code>gometalinter</code>. It is 2-7x faster than <code>gometalinter</code> <a href="https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/#comparison">along with a host of other benefits</a>.</p>
<p>golangci-lint is a powerful, customizable aggregator of linters. By default, several are enabled but not all. A full list of linters and their usages can be found <a href="https://github.com/golangci/awesome-go-linters">here</a>.</p>
<p>It will allow you to configure each linter and choose which ones you would like to enable in your project.</p>
<p>One awesome feature of <code>golangci-lint</code> is that is can be easily introduced to an existing large codebase using the <code>--new-from-rev COMMITID</code>. With this setting only newly introduced issues are flagged, allowing a team to improve new code without having to fix all historic issues in a large codebase. This provides a great path to improving code-reviews on existing solutions. golangci-lint can also be setup as the default linter in VS Code.</p>
<p>Installation options for golangci-lint are present at <a href="https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint#binary">golangci-lint</a>.</p>
<p>To use golangci-lint with VS Code, use the below recommended settings:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">&quot;go.lintTool&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="s2">&quot;golangci-lint&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">   </span><span class="nt">&quot;go.lintFlags&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">     </span><span class="s2">&quot;--fast&quot;</span>
<span class="w">   </span><span class="p">]</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="pre-commit-hooks">Pre-Commit Hooks</h2>
<p>All developers should run <code>gofmt</code> in a pre-commit hook to ensure standard formatting.</p>
<h3 id="step-1-install-pre-commit">Step 1- Install pre-commit</h3>
<p>Run <code>pip install pre-commit</code> to install pre-commit.
Alternatively you can run <code>brew install pre-commit</code> if you are using homebrew.</p>
<h3 id="step-2-add-go-fmt-in-pre-commit">Step 2- Add go-fmt in pre-commit</h3>
<p>Add .pre-commit-config.yaml file to root of the go project. Run go-fmt on pre-commit by adding it to .pre-commit-config.yaml file like below.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">repo</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">git://github.com/dnephin/pre-commit-golang</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">rev</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">master</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">hooks</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">id</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">go-fmt</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="step-3">Step 3</h3>
<p>Run <code>$ pre-commit install</code> to set up the git hook scripts</p>
<h2 id="build-validation">Build Validation</h2>
<p><code>gofmt</code> should be run as a part of every build to enforce the common standard.</p>
<p>To automate this process in Azure DevOps you can add the following snippet to your <code>azure-pipelines.yaml</code> file. This will format any scripts in the <code>./scripts/</code> folder.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">go fmt</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">workingDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/scripts</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;Run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">code</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">formatting&quot;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p><code>govet</code> should be run as a part of every build to check code linting.</p>
<p>To automate this process in Azure DevOps you can add the following snippet to your <code>azure-pipelines.yaml</code> file. This will check linting of any scripts in the <code>./scripts/</code> folder.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">go vet</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">workingDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/scripts</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;Run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">code</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">linting&quot;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>Alternatively you can use golangci-lint as a step in the pipeline to do multiple enabled validations(including go vet and go fmt) of golangci-lint.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">golangci-lint run --enable gofmt --fix</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">workingDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/scripts</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;Run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">code</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">linting&quot;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="sample-build-validation-pipeline-in-azure-devops">Sample Build Validation Pipeline in Azure DevOps</h2>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">trigger</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">master</span>

<span class="nt">pool</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">   </span><span class="nt">vmImage</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;ubuntu-latest&#39;</span>

<span class="nt">steps</span><span class="p">:</span>

<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">GoTool@0</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;1.13.5&#39;</span>

<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Go@0</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">command</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;get&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">arguments</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;-d&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">workingDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/scripts&#39;</span>


<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">go fmt</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">workingDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/scripts</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;Run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">code</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">formatting&quot;</span>

<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">go vet</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">workingDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/scripts</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">go</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">vet&#39;</span>

<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Go@0</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">command</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;build&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">workingDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)&#39;</span>

<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">CopyFiles@2</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">TargetFolder</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)&#39;</span>
<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">PublishBuildArtifacts@1</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">     </span><span class="nt">artifactName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">drop</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="code-review-checklist">Code Review Checklist</h2>
<p>The Go language team maintains a list of common <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments">Code Review Comments</a> for go that form the basis for a solid checklist for a team working in Go that should be followed in addition to the <a href="../../process-guidance/reviewer-guidance/">ISE Code Review Checklist</a></p>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code <a href="https://golang.org/doc/effective_go.html#errors">handle errors</a> correctly? This includes not throwing away errors with <code>_</code> assignments and returning errors, instead of <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#in-band-errors">in-band error values</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code follow Go standards for method <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#receiver-type">receiver types</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#pass-values">pass values</a> when it should?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are interfaces in this code defined in the <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#interfaces">correct packages</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Do go-routines in this code have <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#goroutine-lifetimes">clear lifetimes</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is parallelism in this code handled via go-routines and channels with <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#synchronous-functions">synchronous methods</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code have meaningful <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#doc-comments">Doc Comments</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code have meaningful <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#package-comments">Package Comments</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does this code use <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#contexts">Contexts</a> correctly?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Do unit tests fail with <a href="https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CodeReviewComments#useful-test-failures">meaningful messages</a>?</li>
</ul>

<h1 id="java-code-reviews">Java Code Reviews</h1>
<h2 id="java-style-guide">Java Style Guide</h2>
<p>Developers should follow the <a href="https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html">Google Java Style Guide</a>.</p>
<h2 id="code-analysis-linting">Code Analysis / Linting</h2>
<p>We strongly believe that consistent style increases readability and maintainability of a code base. Hence, we are recommending analyzers to enforce consistency and style rules.</p>
<p>We make use of <a href="https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle">Checkstyle</a> using the <a href="https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-java/blob/master/eng/code-quality-reports/src/main/resources/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml">same configuration used in the Azure Java SDK</a>.</p>
<p><a href="http://findbugs.sourceforge.net/">FindBugs</a> and <a href="https://pmd.github.io/">PMD</a> are also commonly used.</p>
<h2 id="automatic-code-formatting">Automatic Code Formatting</h2>
<p>Eclipse, and other Java IDEs, support automatic code formatting.  If using Maven, some developers also make use of the <a href="https://github.com/revelc/formatter-maven-plugin">formatter-maven-plugin</a>.</p>
<h2 id="build-validation">Build Validation</h2>
<p>It's important to enforce your code style and rules in the CI to avoid any team members merging code that does not comply with standards into your git repo.  If building using Azure DevOps, Azure DevOps support <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/build/maven?view=azure-devops">Maven</a> and <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/build/gradle?view=azure-devops">Gradle</a> build tasks using <a href="https://pmd.github.io/">PMD</a>, <a href="https://checkstyle.sourceforge.io/">Checkstyle</a>, and <a href="http://findbugs.sourceforge.net/">FindBugs</a> code analysis tools as part of every build.</p>
<p>Here is an example yaml for a Maven build task with all three analysis tools enabled:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Maven@3</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Maven</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">pom.xml&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">mavenPomFile</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;$(Parameters.mavenPOMFile)&#39;</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">checkStyleRunAnalysis</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">true</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">pmdRunAnalysis</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">true</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">findBugsRunAnalysis</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">true</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>Here is an example yaml for a Gradle build task with all three analysis tools enabled:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Gradle@2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;gradlew</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">build&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">checkStyleRunAnalysis</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">true</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">findBugsRunAnalysis</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">true</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">pmdRunAnalysis</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">true</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="code-review-checklist">Code Review Checklist</h2>
<p>In addition to the <a href="../../process-guidance/reviewer-guidance/">Code Review Checklist</a> you should also look for these Java specific code review items</p>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does the project use Lambda to make code cleaner?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is dependency injection (DI) used?  Is it setup correctly?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> If the code uses Spring Boot, are you using @Inject instead of @Autowire?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does the code handle exceptions correctly?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/java/azure/jdk/java-jdk-install?view=azure-java-stable">Azul Zulu OpenJDK</a> being used?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is a build automation and package management tool (Gradle or Maven) being used?</li>
</ul>

<h1 id="javascripttypescript-code-reviews">JavaScript/TypeScript Code Reviews</h1>
<h2 id="style-guide">Style Guide</h2>
<p>Developers should use <a href="https://prettier.io/">prettier</a> to do code formatting for JavaScript.</p>
<p>Using an automated code formatting tool like Prettier enforces a well accepted style guide that was collaboratively built by a wide range of companies including Microsoft, Facebook, and AirBnB.</p>
<p>For higher level style guidance not covered by prettier, we follow the <a href="https://github.com/airbnb/javascript">AirBnB Style Guide</a>.</p>
<h2 id="code-analysis-linting">Code Analysis / Linting</h2>
<h3 id="eslint">eslint</h3>
<p>Per guidance outlined in <a href="https://medium.com/palantir/tslint-in-2019-1a144c2317a9">Palantir's 2019 TSLint road map</a>,
TypeScript code should be linted with <a href="https://github.com/eslint/eslint">ESLint</a>. See the <a href="https://typescript-eslint.io/">typescript-eslint</a> documentation for more information around linting TypeScript code with ESLint.</p>
<p>To <a href="https://typescript-eslint.io/">install and configure linting with ESLint</a>,
install the following packages as dev-dependencies:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>npm<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>-D<span class="w"> </span>eslint<span class="w"> </span>@typescript-eslint/parser<span class="w"> </span>@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin
</code></pre></div>
<p>Add a <code>.eslintrc.js</code> to the root of your project:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nx">module</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">exports</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nx">root</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nx">parser</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s1">&#39;@typescript-eslint/parser&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nx">plugins</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;@typescript-eslint&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">],</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">extends</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;eslint:recommended&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;plugin:@typescript-eslint/eslint-recommended&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">],</span>
<span class="p">};</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>Add the following to the <code>scripts</code> of your <code>package.json</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">&quot;scripts&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&quot;lint&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;eslint . --ext .js,.jsx,.ts,.tsx --ignore-path .gitignore&quot;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>This will lint all <code>.js</code>, <code>.jsx</code>, <code>.ts</code>, <code>.tsx</code> files in your project and omit any files or
directories specified in your <code>.gitignore</code>.</p>
<p>You can run linting with:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>npm<span class="w"> </span>run<span class="w"> </span>lint
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="setting-up-prettier">Setting up Prettier</h2>
<p><a href="https://prettier.io/docs/en/">Prettier</a> is an opinionated code formatter.</p>
<p><a href="https://prettier.io/docs/en/integrating-with-linters.html">Getting started guide</a>.</p>
<p>Install with <code>npm</code> as a dev-dependency:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>npm<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>-D<span class="w"> </span>prettier<span class="w"> </span>eslint-config-prettier<span class="w"> </span>eslint-plugin-prettier
</code></pre></div>
<p>Add <code>prettier</code> to your <code>.eslintrc.js</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nx">module</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">exports</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nx">root</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nx">parser</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s1">&#39;@typescript-eslint/parser&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nx">plugins</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;@typescript-eslint&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">],</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="k">extends</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;eslint:recommended&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;plugin:@typescript-eslint/eslint-recommended&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;prettier/@typescript-eslint&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="s1">&#39;plugin:prettier/recommended&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">],</span>
<span class="p">};</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>This will apply the <code>prettier</code> rule set when linting with ESLint.</p>
<h2 id="auto-formatting-with-vscode">Auto Formatting with VSCode</h2>
<p>VS Code can be configured to automatically perform <code>eslint --fix</code> on save.</p>
<p>Create a <code>.vscode</code> folder in the root of your project and add the following to your
<code>.vscode/settings.json</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">&quot;editor.codeActionsOnSave&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&quot;source.fixAll.eslint&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>By default, we use the following overrides should be added to the VS Code configuration to standardize on single quotes, a four space drop, and to do ESLinting:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&quot;prettier.singleQuote&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&quot;prettier.eslintIntegration&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">&quot;prettier.tabWidth&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="setting-up-testing">Setting Up Testing</h2>
<p>Playwright is highly recommended to be set up within a project. its an open source testing suite created by Microsoft.</p>
<p>To install it use this command:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>npm<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>playwright
</code></pre></div>
<p>Since playwright shows the tests in the browser you have to choose which browser you want it to run if unless using chrome, which is the default. You can do this by</p>
<h2 id="build-validation">Build Validation</h2>
<p>To automate this process in Azure Devops you can add the following snippet to your pipeline definition yaml file. This will lint any scripts in the <code>./scripts/</code> folder.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Npm@1</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Lint&#39;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">command</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;custom&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">customCommand</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">lint&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">workingDir</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;./scripts/&#39;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="pre-commit-hooks">Pre-Commit Hooks</h2>
<p>All developers should run <code>eslint</code> in a pre-commit hook to ensure standard formatting. We highly recommend using an editor integration like <a href="https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode-eslint">vscode-eslint</a> to provide realtime feedback.</p>
<ol>
<li>Under <code>.git/hooks</code> rename <code>pre-commit.sample</code> to <code>pre-commit</code></li>
<li>Remove the existing sample code in that file</li>
<li>There are many examples of scripts for this on gist, like <a href="https://gist.github.com/linhmtran168/2286aeafe747e78f53bf">pre-commit-eslint</a></li>
<li>Modify accordingly to include TypeScript files (include ts extension and make sure typescript-eslint is set up)</li>
<li>Make the file executable: <code>chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit</code></li>
</ol>
<p>As an alternative <a href="https://github.com/typicode/husky">husky</a> can be considered to simplify pre-commit hooks.</p>
<h2 id="code-review-checklist">Code Review Checklist</h2>
<p>In addition to the <a href="../../process-guidance/reviewer-guidance/">Code Review Checklist</a> you should also look for these JavaScript and TypeScript specific code review items.</p>
<h3 id="javascript-typescript-checklist">Javascript / Typescript Checklist</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does the code stick to our formatting and code standards? Does running prettier and ESLint over the code should yield no warnings or errors respectively?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does the change re-implement code that would be better served by pulling in a well known module from the ecosystem?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is <code>"use strict";</code> used to reduce errors with undeclared variables?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are unit tests used where possible, also for APIs?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are tests arranged correctly with the <strong>Arrange/Act/Assert</strong> pattern and properly documented in this way?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are best practices for error handling followed, as well as <code>try catch finally</code> statements?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are the <code>doWork().then(doSomething).then(checkSomething)</code> properly followed for async calls, including <code>expect</code>, <code>done</code>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Instead of using raw strings, are constants used in the main class? Or if these strings are used across files/classes, is there a static class for the constants?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are magic numbers explained? There should be no number in the code without at least a comment of why it is there. If the number is repetitive, is there a constant/enum or equivalent?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> If there is an asynchronous method, does the name of the method end with the <code>Async</code> suffix?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is a minimum level of logging in place? Are the logging levels used sensible?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is document fragment manipulation limited to when you need to manipulate multiple sub elements?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does TypeScript code compile without raising linting errors?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Instead of using raw strings, are constants used in the main class? Or if these strings are used across files/classes, is there a static class for the constants?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are magic numbers explained? There should be no number in the code without at least a comment of why it is there. If the number is repetitive, is there a constant/enum or equivalent?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is there a proper <code>/* */</code> in the various classes and methods?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are heavy operations implemented in the backend, leaving the controller as thin as possible?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is event handling on the html efficiently done?</li>
</ul>

<h1 id="markdown-code-reviews">Markdown Code Reviews</h1>
<h2 id="style-guide">Style Guide</h2>
<p>Developers should treat documentation like other source code and follow the same rules and checklists when reviewing documentation as code.</p>
<p>Documentation should both use good Markdown syntax to ensure it's properly parsed, and follow good <a href="#writing-style-guidelines">writing style guidelines</a> to ensure the document is easy to read and understand.</p>
<h2 id="markdown">Markdown</h2>
<p>Markdown is a lightweight markup language that you can use to add formatting elements to plaintext text documents. Created by John Gruber in 2004, Markdown is now one of the world’s most popular markup languages.</p>
<p>Using Markdown is different from using a WYSIWYG editor. In an application like Microsoft Word, you click buttons to format words and phrases, and the changes are visible immediately. Markdown isn’t like that. When you create a Markdown-formatted file, you add Markdown syntax to the text to indicate which words and phrases should look different.</p>
<p>You can find more information and full documentation <a href="https://www.markdownguide.org/">here</a>.</p>
<h2 id="linters">Linters</h2>
<p>Markdown has specific way of being formatted. It is important to respect this formatting, otherwise some interpreters which are strict won't properly display the document. Linters are often used to help developers properly create documents by both verifying proper Markdown syntax, grammar and proper English language.</p>
<p>A good setup includes a markdown linter used during editing and PR build verification, and a grammar linter used while editing the document. The following are a list of linters that could be used in this setup.</p>
<h3 id="markdownlint">markdownlint</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/markdownlint/markdownlint"><code>markdownlint</code></a> is a linter for markdown that verifies Markdown syntax, and also enforces rules that make the text more readable. <a href="https://github.com/igorshubovych/markdownlint-cli">Markdownlint-cli</a> is an easy-to-use CLI based on Markdownlint.</p>
<p>It's available as a <a href="https://github.com/markdownlint/markdownlint">ruby gem</a>, an <a href="https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint">npm package</a>, a <a href="https://github.com/igorshubovych/markdownlint-cli">Node.js CLI</a> and a <a href="https://github.com/DavidAnson/vscode-markdownlint">VS Code extension</a>. The VS Code extension <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=esbenp.prettier-vscode">Prettier</a> also catches all markdownlint errors.</p>
<p>Installing the Node.js CLI</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>npm<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>-g<span class="w"> </span>markdownlint-cli
</code></pre></div>
<p>Running markdownlint on a Node.js project</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>markdownlint<span class="w"> </span>**/*.md<span class="w"> </span>--ignore<span class="w"> </span>node_modules
</code></pre></div>
<p>Fixing errors automatically</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>markdownlint<span class="w"> </span>**/*.md<span class="w"> </span>--ignore<span class="w"> </span>node_modules<span class="w"> </span>--fix
</code></pre></div>
<p>A comprehensive list of markdownlint rules is available <a href="https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint/blob/main/doc/Rules.md">here</a>.</p>
<h3 id="write-good">write-good</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/btford/write-good"><code>write-good</code></a> is a linter for English text that helps writing better documentation.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>npm<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>-g<span class="w"> </span>write-good
</code></pre></div>
<p>Run write-good</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>write-good<span class="w"> </span>*.md
</code></pre></div>
<p>Run write-good without installing it</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>npx<span class="w"> </span>write-good<span class="w"> </span>*.md
</code></pre></div>
<p>Write Good is also available as an <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=travisthetechie.write-good-linter">extension for VS Code</a></p>
<h2 id="vscode-extensions">VSCode Extensions</h2>
<h3 id="write-good-linter">Write Good Linter</h3>
<p>The <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=travisthetechie.write-good-linter"><code>Write Good Linter Extension</code></a> integrates with VS Code to give grammar and language advice while editing the document.</p>
<h3 id="markdownlint-extension">markdownlint Extension</h3>
<p>The <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=DavidAnson.vscode-markdownlint"><code>markdownlint extension</code></a> examines the Markdown documents, showing warnings for rule violations while editing.</p>
<h2 id="build-validation">Build Validation</h2>
<h3 id="linting">Linting</h3>
<p>To automate linting with <code>markdownlint</code> for PR validation in GitHub actions,
you can either use linters aggregator as we do with <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/code-with-engineering-playbook/blob/main/.github/workflows/mega-linter.yml">MegaLinter in this repository</a> or use the following YAML.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Markdownlint</span>

<span class="nt">on</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">push</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">paths</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;**/*.md&quot;</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">pull_request</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">paths</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&quot;**/*.md&quot;</span>

<span class="nt">jobs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">lint</span><span class="p">:</span>

<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">runs-on</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">ubuntu-latest</span>

<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">steps</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">uses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">actions/checkout@v2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Use Node.js</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">uses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">actions/setup-node@v1</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">with</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">node-version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">12.x</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Run Markdownlint</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">run</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p p-Indicator">|</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="no">npm i -g markdownlint-cli</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="no">markdownlint &quot;**/*.md&quot; --ignore node_modules</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="checking-links">Checking Links</h3>
<p>To automate link check in your markdown files add <code>lycheeverse/lychee-action</code> action to your validation pipeline:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">markdown-link-check</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">runs-on</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">ubuntu-latest</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">steps</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">uses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">actions/checkout@v4</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Link Checker</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">id</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">lychee</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">uses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>More information about this action options can be found at <a href="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action"><code>lychee-action</code> home page</a>.</p>
<h2 id="code-review-checklist">Code Review Checklist</h2>
<p>In addition to the <a href="../../process-guidance/reviewer-guidance/">Code Review Checklist</a> you should also look for these documentation specific code review items</p>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the document easy to read and understand and does it follow <a href="#writing-style-guidelines">good writing guidelines</a>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is there a single source of truth or is content repeated in more than one document?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the documentation up to date with the code?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the documentation technically, and ethically correct?</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="writing-style-guidelines">Writing Style Guidelines</h2>
<p>The following are some examples of writing style guidelines.</p>
<p>Agree in your team which guidelines you should apply to your project documentation.
Save your guidelines together with your documentation, so they are easy to refer back to.</p>
<h3 id="wording">Wording</h3>
<ul>
<li>Use inclusive language, and avoid jargon and uncommon words. The docs should be easy to understand</li>
<li>Be clear and concise, stick to the goal of the document</li>
<li>Use active voice</li>
<li>Spell check and grammar check the text</li>
<li>Always follow chronological order</li>
<li>Visit <a href="https://plainenglish.co.uk/how-to-write-in-plain-english.html">Plain English</a> for tips on how to write documentation that is easy to understand.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="document-organization">Document Organization</h3>
<ul>
<li>Organize documents by topic rather than type, this makes it easier to find the documentation</li>
<li>Each folder should have a top-level README.md and any other documents within that folder should link directly or indirectly from that README.md</li>
<li>Document names with more than one word should use underscores instead of spaces, for example <code>machine_learning_pipeline_design.md</code>. The same applies to images</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="headings">Headings</h3>
<ul>
<li>Start with a H1 (single # in markdown) and respect the order H1 &gt; H2 &gt; H3 etc</li>
<li>Follow each heading with text before proceeding with the next heading</li>
<li>Avoid putting numbers in headings. Numbers shift, and can create outdated titles</li>
<li>Avoid using symbols and special characters in headers, this causes problems with anchor links</li>
<li>Avoid links in headers</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="resources">Resources</h3>
<ul>
<li>Avoid duplication of content, instead link to the <code>single source of truth</code></li>
<li>Link but don't summarize. Summarizing content on another page leads to the content living in two places</li>
<li>Use meaningful anchor texts, e.g. instead of writing <code>Follow the instructions [here](../recipes/markdown.md)</code> write <code>Follow the [Markdown guidelines](../recipes/markdown.md)</code></li>
<li>Make sure links to Microsoft docs do not contain the language marker <code>/en-us/</code> or <code>/fr-fr/</code>, as this is automatically determined by the site itself.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="lists">Lists</h3>
<ul>
<li>List items should start with capital letters if possible</li>
<li>Use ordered lists when the items describe a sequence to follow, otherwise use unordered lists</li>
<li>For ordered lists, prefix each item with <code>1.</code> When rendered, the list items will appear with sequential numbering. This avoids number-gaps in list</li>
<li>Do not add commas <code>,</code> or semicolons <code>;</code> to the end of list items, and avoid periods <code>.</code> unless the list item represents a complete sentence</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="images">Images</h3>
<ul>
<li>Place images in a separate directory named <code>img</code></li>
<li>Name images appropriately, avoiding generic names like <code>screenshot.png</code></li>
<li>Avoid adding large images or videos to source control, link to an external location instead</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="emphasis-and-special-sections">Emphasis and Special Sections</h3>
<ul>
<li>Use <strong>bold</strong> or <em>italic</em> to emphasize<blockquote>
<p>For sections that everyone reading this document needs to be aware of, use blocks</p>
</blockquote>
</li>
<li>
<p>Use <code>backticks</code> for code, a single backtick for inline code like <code>pip install flake8</code> and 3 backticks for code blocks followed by the language for syntax highlighting</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">add</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">num1</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">num2</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">):</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">num1</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">num2</span>
</code></pre></div>
</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li>Use check boxes for task lists<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Item 1</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Item 2</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled checked/> Item 3</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Add a References section to the end of the document with links to external references</li>
<li>
<p>Prefer tables to lists for comparisons and reports to make research and results more readable</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Option</th>
<th>Pros</th>
<th>Cons</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Option 1</td>
<td>Some pros</td>
<td>Some cons</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Option 2</td>
<td>Some pros</td>
<td>Some cons</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="general">General</h3>
<ul>
<li>Always use Markdown syntax, don't mix with HTML</li>
<li>Make sure the extension of the files is <code>.md</code> - if the extension is missing, a linter might ignore the files</li>
</ul>
