<h1 id="python-code-reviews">Python Code Reviews</h1>
<h2 id="style-guide">Style Guide</h2>
<p>Developers should follow the <a href="https://pep8.org/">PEP8 style guide</a> with <a href="https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/">type hints</a>. The use of type hints throughout paired with linting and type hint checking avoids common errors that are tricky to debug.</p>
<p>Projects should check Python code with automated tools.</p>
<p>Linting should be added to build validation, and both linting and code formatting can be added to your pre-commit hooks and VS Code.</p>
<h2 id="code-analysis-linting">Code Analysis / Linting</h2>
<p>The 2 most popular python linters are <a href="https://pypi.org/project/pylint/">Pylint</a> and <a href="https://pypi.org/project/flake8/">Flake8</a>. Both check adherence to <code>PEP8</code> but vary a bit in what other rules they check. In general <code>Pylint</code> tends to be a bit more stringent and give more false positives but both are good options for linting python code.</p>
<p>Both <code>Pylint</code> and <code>Flake8</code> can be configured in VS Code using the VS Code <code>python extension</code>.</p>
<h3 id="flake8">Flake8</h3>
<p>Flake8 is a simple and fast wrapper around <a href="https://github.com/PyCQA/pyflakes"><code>Pyflakes</code></a> (for detecting coding errors) and <a href="https://github.com/PyCQA/pycodestyle"><code>pycodestyle</code></a> (for pep8).</p>
<p>Install <code>Flake8</code></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>flake8
</code></pre></div>
<p>Add an extension for the <a href="https://github.com/PyCQA/pydocstyle"><code>pydocstyle</code></a> (for <a href="https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0257/">doc strings</a>) tool to flake8.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>flake8-docstrings
</code></pre></div>
<p>Add an extension for <a href="https://github.com/PyCQA/pep8-naming"><code>pep8-naming</code></a> (for <a href="https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/#naming-conventions">naming conventions</a> in pep8) tool to flake8.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>pep8-naming
</code></pre></div>
<p>Run <code>Flake8</code></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>flake8<span class="w"> </span>.<span class="w">    </span><span class="c1"># lint the whole project</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="pylint">Pylint</h3>
<p>Install <code>Pylint</code></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>pylint
</code></pre></div>
<p>Run <code>Pylint</code></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pylint<span class="w"> </span>src<span class="w">  </span><span class="c1"># lint the source directory</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="automatic-code-formatting">Automatic Code Formatting</h2>
<h3 id="black">Black</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/psf/black"><code>Black</code></a> is an unapologetic code formatting tool. It removes all need from <code>pycodestyle</code> nagging about formatting, so the team can focus on content vs style. It's not possible to configure black for your own style needs.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>black
</code></pre></div>
<p>Format python code</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>black<span class="w"> </span><span class="o">[</span>file/folder<span class="o">]</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="autopep8">autopep8</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/hhatto/autopep8"><code>Autopep8</code></a> is more lenient and allows more configuration if you want less stringent formatting.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>autopep8
</code></pre></div>
<p>Format python code</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>autopep8<span class="w"> </span><span class="o">[</span>file/folder<span class="o">]</span><span class="w"> </span>--in-place
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="yapf">yapf</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/google/yapf">yapf</a> Yet Another Python Formatter is a python formatter from Google based on ideas from gofmt.  This is also more configurable, and a good option for automatic code formatting.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>yapf
</code></pre></div>
<p>Format python code</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>yapf<span class="w"> </span><span class="o">[</span>file/folder<span class="o">]</span><span class="w"> </span>--in-place
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="bandit">Bandit</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/PyCQA/bandit">Bandit</a> is a tool designed by the Python Code Quality Authority (PyCQA) to perform static analysis of Python code, specifically targeting security issues.
It scans for common security issues in Python codebase.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Installation</strong>: Add Bandit to your development environment with:
  <div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>bandit
</code></pre></div></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="vscode-extensions">VSCode Extensions</h2>
<h3 id="python">Python</h3>
<p>The <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-python.python"><code>Python language extension</code></a> is the base extension you should have installed for python development with VS Code. It enables intellisense, debugging, linting (with the above linters), testing with pytest or unittest, and code formatting with the formatters mentioned above.</p>
<h3 id="pyright">Pyright</h3>
<p>The <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-pyright.pyright"><code>Pyright extension</code></a> augments VS Code with static type checking when you use type hints</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="k">def</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">add</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">first_value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">second_value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">first_value</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">second_value</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="build-validation">Build Validation</h2>
<p>To automate linting with <code>flake8</code> and testing with <code>pytest</code> in Azure Devops you can add the following snippet to you <code>azure-pipelines.yaml</code> file.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">trigger</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">branches</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">include</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">develop</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">master</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">paths</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">include</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">src/*</span>

<span class="nt">pool</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">vmImage</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;ubuntu-latest&#39;</span>

<span class="nt">jobs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">job</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">LintAndTest</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">Lint and Test</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">steps</span><span class="p">:</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">checkout</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">self</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">lfs</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">true</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">UsePythonVersion@0</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Set</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">Python</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">version</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">to</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">3.6&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">versionSpec</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;3.6&#39;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">pip3 install --user -r requirements.txt</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Install</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">dependencies&#39;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p p-Indicator">|</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="no"># Install Flake8</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="no">pip3 install --user flake8</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="no"># Install PyTest</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="no">pip3 install --user pytest</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Install</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">Flake8</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">and</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">PyTest&#39;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p p-Indicator">|</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="no">python3 -m flake8</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">Flake8</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">linter&#39;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">script</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p p-Indicator">|</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="no"># Run PyTest tester</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="no">python3 -m pytest --junitxml=./test-results.xml</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Run</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">PyTest</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">Tester&#39;</span>

<span class="w">  </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">task</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">PublishTestResults@2</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">displayName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Publish</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">PyTest</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">results&#39;</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">condition</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">succeededOrFailed()</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">testResultsFiles</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;**/test-*.xml&#39;</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">testRunTitle</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">&#39;Publish</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">test</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">results</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">for</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">Python</span><span class="nv"> </span><span class="s">$(python.version)&#39;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>To perform a PR validation on GitHub you can use a similar YAML configuration with <a href="https://help.github.com/en/actions/language-and-framework-guides/using-python-with-github-actions">GitHub Actions</a></p>
<h2 id="pre-commit-hooks">Pre-Commit Hooks</h2>
<p>Pre-commit hooks allow you to format and lint code locally before submitting the pull request.</p>
<p>Adding pre-commit hooks for your python repository is easy using the pre-commit package</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Install pre-commit and add to the requirements.txt</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pip<span class="w"> </span>install<span class="w"> </span>pre-commit
</code></pre></div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Add a <code>.pre-commit-config.yaml</code> file in the root of the repository, with the desired pre-commit actions</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="nt">repos</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="nt">repo</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">https://github.com/ambv/black</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">rev</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">stable</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">hooks</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">id</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">black</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">language_version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">python3.6</span>
<span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="nt">repo</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">rev</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">v1.2.3</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">hooks</span><span class="p">:</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p p-Indicator">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">id</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l l-Scalar l-Scalar-Plain">flake8</span>
</code></pre></div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Each individual developer that wants to set up pre-commit hooks can then run</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code>pre-commit<span class="w"> </span>install
</code></pre></div>
</li>
</ol>
<p>At the next attempted commit any lint failures will block the commit.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Note: Installing pre-commit hooks is voluntary and done by each developer individually. Thus, it's not a replacement for build validation on the server</p>
</blockquote>
<h2 id="code-review-checklist">Code Review Checklist</h2>
<p>In addition to the <a href="../../process-guidance/reviewer-guidance/">Code Review Checklist</a> you should also look for these python specific code review items</p>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are all new packages used included in requirements.txt</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Does the code pass all lint checks?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Do functions use type hints, and are there any type hint errors?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Is the code readable and using pythonic constructs wherever possible.</li>
</ul>

<h1 id="terraform-code-reviews">Terraform Code Reviews</h1>
<h2 id="style-guide">Style Guide</h2>
<p>Developers should follow the <a href="https://github.com/jonbrouse/terraform-style-guide/blob/master/README.md">terraform style guide</a>.</p>
<p>Projects should check Terraform scripts with automated tools.</p>
<h2 id="code-analysis-linting">Code Analysis / Linting</h2>
<h3 id="tflint">TFLint</h3>
<p><a href="https://github.com/terraform-linters/tflint"><code>TFLint</code></a> is a Terraform linter focused on possible errors, best practices, etc. Once TFLint installed in the environment, it can be invoked using the VS Code <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=mauve.terraform"><code>terraform extension</code></a>.</p>
<h2 id="vscode-extensions">VSCode Extensions</h2>
<p>The following VS Code extensions are widely used.</p>
<h3 id="terraform-extension"><a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=mauve.terraform"><code>Terraform extension</code></a></h3>
<p>This extension provides syntax highlighting, linting, formatting and validation capabilities.</p>
<h3 id="azure-terraform-extension"><a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-azuretools.vscode-azureterraform"><code>Azure Terraform extension</code></a></h3>
<p>This extension provides Terraform command support, resource graph visualization and CloudShell integration inside VS Code.</p>
<h2 id="build-validation">Build Validation</h2>
<p>Ensure you enforce the style guides during build. The following example script can be used to install terraform, and a linter that
then checks for formatting and common errors.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><span class="ch">#! /bin/bash</span>
<span class="nb">set</span><span class="w"> </span>-e

<span class="nv">SCRIPT_DIR</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="k">$(</span>dirname<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;</span><span class="nv">$BASH_SOURCE</span><span class="s2">&quot;</span><span class="k">)</span>
<span class="nb">cd</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;</span><span class="nv">$SCRIPT_DIR</span><span class="s2">&quot;</span>

<span class="nv">TF_VERSION</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="m">0</span>.12.4
<span class="nv">TF_LINT_VERSION</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="m">0</span>.9.1

<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span>-e<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt; Installing Terraform 0.12&quot;</span>
<span class="c1"># Install terraform tooling for linting terraform</span>
wget<span class="w"> </span>-q<span class="w"> </span>https://releases.hashicorp.com/terraform/<span class="si">${</span><span class="nv">TF_VERSION</span><span class="si">}</span>/terraform_<span class="si">${</span><span class="nv">TF_VERSION</span><span class="si">}</span>_linux_amd64.zip<span class="w"> </span>-O<span class="w"> </span>/tmp/terraform.zip
sudo<span class="w"> </span>unzip<span class="w"> </span>-q<span class="w"> </span>-o<span class="w"> </span>-d<span class="w"> </span>/usr/local/bin/<span class="w"> </span>/tmp/terraform.zip

<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;&quot;</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span>-e<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt; Install tflint (3rd party)&quot;</span>
wget<span class="w"> </span>-q<span class="w"> </span>https://github.com/wata727/tflint/releases/download/v<span class="si">${</span><span class="nv">TF_LINT_VERSION</span><span class="si">}</span>/tflint_linux_amd64.zip<span class="w"> </span>-O<span class="w"> </span>/tmp/tflint.zip
sudo<span class="w"> </span>unzip<span class="w"> </span>-q<span class="w"> </span>-o<span class="w"> </span>-d<span class="w"> </span>/usr/local/bin/<span class="w"> </span>/tmp/tflint.zip

<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span>-e<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt; Terraform version&quot;</span>
terraform<span class="w"> </span>-version

<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span>-e<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt; Terraform Format (if this fails use &#39;terraform fmt -recursive&#39; command to resolve&quot;</span>
terraform<span class="w"> </span>fmt<span class="w"> </span>-recursive<span class="w"> </span>-diff<span class="w"> </span>-check

<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span>-e<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt; tflint&quot;</span>
tflint

<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span>-e<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt; Terraform init&quot;</span>
terraform<span class="w"> </span>init

<span class="nb">echo</span><span class="w"> </span>-e<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt; Terraform validate&quot;</span>
terraform<span class="w"> </span>validate
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="code-review-checklist">Code Review Checklist</h2>
<p>In addition to the <a href="../../process-guidance/reviewer-guidance/">Code Review Checklist</a> you should also look for these Terraform specific code review items</p>
<h3 id="providers">Providers</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Are all providers used in the terraform scripts <a href="https://www.terraform.io/language/providers/requirements#best-practices-for-provider-versions">versioned</a> to prevent breaking changes in the future?</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="repository-organization">Repository Organization</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The code split into reusable modules?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Modules are split into separate <code>.tf</code> files where appropriate?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The repository contains a <code>README.md</code> describing the architecture provisioned?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> If Terraform code is mixed with application source code, the Terraform code isolated into a dedicated folder?</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="terraform-state">Terraform State</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The Terraform project configured using Azure Storage as remote state backend?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The remote state backend storage account key stored a secure location (e.g. Azure Key Vault)?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The project is configured to use state files based on the environment, and the deployment pipeline is configured to supply the state file name dynamically?</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="variables">Variables</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> If the infrastructure will be different depending on the environment (e.g. Dev, UAT, Production), the environment specific parameters are supplied via a <code>.tfvars</code> file?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> All variables have <code>type</code> information. E.g. a <code>list(string)</code> or <code>string</code>.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> All variables have a <code>description</code> stating the purpose of the variable and its usage.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> <code>default</code> values are not supplied for variables which must be supplied by a user.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="testing">Testing</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Unit and integration tests covering the Terraform code exist (e.g. <a href="https://terratest.gruntwork.io/"><code>Terratest</code></a>, <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/terratest-abstraction"><code>terratest-abstraction</code></a>)?</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="naming-and-code-structure">Naming and Code Structure</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Resource definitions and data sources are used correctly in the Terraform scripts?<ul>
<li><strong>resource:</strong> Indicates to Terraform that the current configuration is in charge of managing the life cycle of the object</li>
<li><strong>data:</strong> Indicates to Terraform that you only want to get a reference to the existing object, but don’t want to manage it as part of this configuration</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The resource names start with their containing provider's name followed by an underscore? e.g. resource from the provider <code>postgresql</code> might be named as <code>postgresql_database</code>?</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The <code>try</code> function is only used with simple attribute references and type conversion functions? Overuse of the <code>try</code> function to suppress errors will lead to a configuration that is hard to understand and maintain.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> Explicit type conversion functions used to normalize types are only returned in module outputs? Explicit type conversions are rarely necessary in Terraform because it will convert types automatically where required.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" disabled/> The <code>Sensitive</code> property on schema set to <code>true</code> for the fields that contains sensitive information? This will prevent the field's values from showing up in CLI output.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="general-recommendations">General Recommendations</h3>
<ul>
<li>Try avoiding nesting sub configuration within resources. Create a separate resource section for resources even though they can be declared as sub-element of a resource. For example, declaring subnets within virtual network vs declaring subnets as a separate resources compared to virtual network on Azure.</li>
<li>Never hard-code any value in configuration. Declare them in <code>locals</code> section if a variable is needed multiple times as a static value and are internal to the configuration.</li>
<li>The <code>name</code>s of the resources created on Azure should not be hard-coded or static. These names should be dynamic and user-provided using <code>variable</code> block. This is helpful especially in unit testing when multiple tests are running in parallel trying to create resources on Azure but need different names (few resources in Azure need to be named uniquely e.g. storage accounts).</li>
<li>It is a good practice to <code>output</code> the ID of resources created on Azure from configuration. This is especially helpful when adding dynamic blocks for sub-elements/child elements to the parent resource.</li>
<li>Use the <code>required_providers</code> block for establishing the dependency for providers along with pre-determined version.</li>
<li>Use the <code>terraform</code> block to declare the provider dependency with exact version and also the terraform CLI version needed for the configuration.</li>
<li>Validate the variable values supplied based on usage and type of variable. The validation can be done to variables by adding <code>validation</code> block.</li>
<li>Validate that the component SKUs are the right ones, e.g. standard vs premium.</li>
</ul>
